<reason>CON won a close, high-quality debate by holding the conjunction: recent switches did not produce the clean surge the motion needs, which PRO conceded on Wales, and a default that cannot be isolated from coordinators is not a proven causal lever. CON also kept a live ethical remainder—silence treated as permission—without needing a complaint spike, and turned the husband example by noting a soft veto still permits refusal. PRO’s bedside-script mechanism and attack on unfalsifiable harm were strong, but never closed the rates burden.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s reply that a rule can be unjust without being effective, then using the soft family veto to show presumed consent neither saves the unregistered husband nor proves a measured gain.</best_rebuttal>
